Day 2 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0100 AM CDT Sat Aug 08 2026

Valid 091200Z - 101200Z

...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS PARTS OF
THE MIDWEST...

...SUMMARY...
Thunderstorms with severe wind gusts will be possible Sunday
afternoon and evening from parts of the northern Plains
east-southeastward into the southern Great Lakes. Severe gusts will
also be possible in parts of the southern Appalachians, Maine and
southeast Arizona.

...Northern Plains/Mid To Upper Mississippi Valley/Southern Great
Lakes...
Mid-level flow will be west-northwesterly on Sunday from the
northern Plains into the Great Lakes. At the surface, a moist and
unstable airmass will be in place from South Dakota eastward into
the southern Great Lakes. Although moderate instability is forecast
to develop over much of this corridor by afternoon, large-scale
ascent will remain relatively weak. For that reason, thunderstorm
development will confined to areas where low-level convergence
becomes maximized. Some solutions show an east-to-west axis of
strong low-level convergence from Iowa into northern Indiana,
suggesting this could be a favored area for thunderstorm development
in the afternoon and evening. 

Forecast soundings near this axis in the late afternoon have surface
dewpoints in the 70s with moderate to strong instability. 0-6 km
shear is forecast to be in the 35 to 45 knot range with a
substantial amount of low-level directional shear. This should
support a severe threat with supercells and short intense line
segments. Severe wind gusts will be the primary threat.

Further west into parts of the northern Plains, a subtle shortwave
trough is forecast to move into South Dakota during the day. A
post-frontal airmass will be in place ahead of the shortwave with
surface dewpoints in the 60s to near 70 F. This will contribute to
moderate instability by afternoon. Thunderstorms that develop near
the axis of instability will have potential for isolated severe
gusts during the late afternoon and early evening.

...Maine...
A mid-level shortwave trough is forecast to move across the Great
Lakes on Sunday, with west-southwesterly flow located over the
Northeast. Ahead of the system, a cold front is forecast to move
eastward across New England. As surface temperatures warm during the
day, thunderstorm development is expected to take place near the
front in the higher terrain across parts of western Maine. These
storms are forecast to move quickly eastward across central and
eastern Maine during the afternoon. Moderate instability, steep low
lapse rates and sufficient deep-layer shear will likely support an
isolated wind-damage threat.

...Southern Appalachians...
Moderate instability will develop on Sunday across much of the
southern Appalachians, where surface dewpoints will be in the upper
60s to mid 70s F. As surface temperatures warm during the day,
scattered thunderstorms will develop in the higher terrain. The
moderate instability, along with precipitable water values in the
1.70 to 1.85 inch range, will support a potential for isolated
severe wet downbursts as instability becomes maximized in the late
afternoon.

...Southeast Arizona...
Surface dewpoints across southern Arizona will be in the upper 50s
to near 60 F on Sunday. As surface temperatures warm during the day,
moderate instability will develop over much of southern Arizona.
Thunderstorms are expected to form in the higher terrain of eastern
Arizona, with the storms moving west-southwestward into the unstable
air during the late afternoon and early evening. Steep low-level
lapse rates and large surface temperature-dewpoint spreads will
support an isolated wind-damage threat.

..Broyles.. 08/08/2026

$$

Day 3 Convective Outlook CORR 1
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0333 PM CDT Fri Aug 07 2026

Valid 091200Z - 101200Z

...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS FROM THE BLACK
HILLS INTO MID-MISSOURI/MISSISSIPPI VALLEYS AND PARTS OF THE
SOUTHERN GREAT LAKES...CENTRAL/EASTERN MAINE...

CORRECTED FOR TYPO

...SUMMARY...
Thunderstorms with isolated severe wind gusts and hail will be
possible Sunday afternoon and evening from parts of the central and
northern Plains east-southeastward into the southern Great Lakes
region. Additional strong to severe storms are possible in Maine.

...Black Hills into parts of the lower Great Lakes...
Forecast uncertainty remains high. A moderate to strong low-level
jet is forecast to persist into early Sunday morning. This feature
will generally be focused into the Mid-Mississippi Valley region. It
is probable that some convection will be ongoing during the early
morning with some risk for large hail and possibly isolated damaging
winds. While the low-level jet will weaken to some extent into the
mid/late morning, modest 850 mb theta-e advection will continue and
may promote stronger development along the outflow from this early
activity. Steep mid-level lapse rates and 40-50 kt of effective
shear on the western flank of the outflow would favor severe storms.
Similar to Saturday, additional storms could form as the low-level
jet intensifies Sunday night. Large hail would be the most likely
hazard as these storms would tend to be slightly elevated.

Farther west, storm development is much more uncertain. Warm
temperatures aloft will lead to capping within the Plains. A surface
low is forecast to develop which may provide local enhancement to
convergence, but the location and strength of this feature varies
model to model. Mid-level ascent will be subtle at best. The ECMWF
is the most aggressive with afternoon development. That solution
suggests development near the surface low/Black Hills with a
southeastward moving complex. While an increase in probabilities
would be needed in this scenario, confidence is not high.

...Maine...
Moderate mid-level winds will continue across much of the Northeast.
Ahead of a cold front, upper 60s to low 70s F dewpoints will support
1500-2000 J/kg MLCAPE. Shear will be modest, but hodographs will be
long. A few marginal supercell structures are possible with an
accompanying risk for isolated wind damage and marginal hail.

..Wendt.. 08/07/2026

$$

Day 4-8 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0359 AM CDT Fri Aug 07 2026

Valid 101200Z - 151200Z

...DISCUSSION...
...Monday/Day 4 to Wednesday/Day 6...
A broad cyclonic flow pattern is forecast to remain in place from
the north-central U.S. to the Northeast during the early to
mid-week. On the southern edge of the stronger flow, it appears that
an east-to-west corridor of moisture and instability will remain in
place from the central Plains eastward into the Midwest. On Monday,
isolated to scattered thunderstorm development will be possible
during the afternoon and evening along and near the northern edge of
the stronger instability, from eastern Nebraska eastward into the
southern Great Lakes. The greatest convective coverage is expected
to be from northern Illinois eastward into western Pennsylvania,
where low-level flow is forecast to be maximized. Moderate
deep-layer shear along this zone is forecast to be favorable for a
severe threat Monday afternoon and evening. Supercells and multicell
line segments will have potential to produce severe wind gusts.

On Tuesday and Wednesday, model forecasts suggest that a front will
move southward into northern sections of the Ohio Valley, while the
instability axis remains in a similar position further west near the
Omaha area. Isolated to scattered thunderstorms will again be
possible in the afternoon and evening, near and to the north of the
instability axis. An isolated severe threat could develop with
storms that form within or near the strongest instability. However,
predictability is low concerning where the greatest potential for
severe storms will be.

...Thursday/Day 7 and Friday/Day 8...
On Thursday and Friday, west to northwesterly mid-level flow is
forecast over much of the eastern half of the nation. A moist and
unstable airmass should be in place from the central and northern
Plains southeastward into the Ohio and Tennessee Valleys. Although
large-scale ascent may be relatively weak over much of this area,
isolated to scattered thunderstorms will be possible across parts of
this airmass during the afternoon and evening. Due to the extended
time range, predictability remains low concerning the finer-scale
details of any scenario from Thursday into Friday.

..Broyles.. 08/07/2026

Day 1 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
1153 PM CDT Fri Aug 07 2026

Valid 081200Z - 091200Z

...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS PORTIONS
OF THE NORTHERN AND CENTRAL PLAINS INTO THE UPPER MISSISSIPPI
VALLEY...PARTS OF THE MID-ATLANTIC...AND SOUTHERN ARIZONA...

...SUMMARY...
Severe thunderstorms will be possible this afternoon and evening
across parts of the central and northern Plains southeastward into
the lower to mid Missouri Valley. Additional strong to severe storms
are possible in the Mid-Atlantic and central/southern Arizona.

...Northern/Central Plains into MN/IA/MO...

A modest but weakening low-level jet across portions of NE/SD may
support ongoing elevated convection this morning, mainly across NE.
This activity will weaken and spread southeast through the morning
hours, but could pose a marginal risk for hail. 

The forecast for the afternoon into nighttime hours becomes complex
and uncertain. Broad northwesterly flow aloft will modestly
strengthen by late afternoon/early evening as several shortwave
impulses migrate through the base of an upper low/trough centered
over central Canada. Height falls are expected to be weak, and warm
mid-level temperatures will pose capping issues. Nevertheless,
surface troughing across the northern/central High Plains will
result in south/southeasterly low-level flow, transporting 60s F
dewpoints northward across the central Plains and MO Valley ahead of
a southward sagging surface front oriented across ND and northern MN
late in the period. Increasing boundary layer moisture beneath steep
midlevel lapse rates will support moderate to strong
destabilization. 

Several areas of convection may develop during the late
afternoon/evening near the surface trough, and overnight near the
southward-sagging surface front. Given weak large-scale ascent and
warm midlevels, it remains uncertain where storm development is most
likely and how storm coverage will evolve. With an increasing
low-level jet across the central Plains during the nighttime hours,
some convection could develop atop a capping inversion, or along the
surface front near the ND/SD border. Isolated large hail is possible
with this activity. If surface-based convection can develop within
the strongly unstable airmass, damaging wind gusts also will be
possible.  

Additional high-based convection is possible across CO and western
KS/NE. A hot and well mixed boundary layer could support strong
outflow winds with this activity as well.

...Mid-Atlantic...

A modest midlevel shortwave trough will overspread the region
through afternoon/early evening. Strong heating of a seasonally
moist airmass will support moderate instability. Vertical shear is
expected to be sufficient for organized cells and clusters with an
attendant risk for damaging wind gusts. The strongest cells could
also produce small hail. 

...AZ...

Easterly midlevel flow will persist on the southern periphery of an
upper high over the Four Corners. Steep midlevel lapse rates and
persistent moisture across the region will foster thunderstorm
development across the higher terrain during the evening. The hot
and well mixed boundary layer will support strong outflow gusts as
convection moves westward off higher terrain toward the lower
deserts.

..Leitman/Marsh.. 08/08/2026
